questions.question: What did the tomb reveal about Egyptian beliefs in the afterlife?
questions.expected_answer: It showed that Egyptians believed the spirit could live forever if the body was preserved and had everything it needed. The king was mummified with natron and linen, his organs placed in tiny golden coffins, and the tomb was filled with food, clothes, furniture, chariots, games, model boats and shabtis to work for him, with paintings of the gods and protective spells.

questions.question: What did the tomb reveal about wealth, skill and trade?
questions.expected_answer: It held more than five thousand objects, many covered in gold, including a solid gold mask and coffin, showing the pharaoh's great wealth, even for a minor king. Fine jewellery, furniture, linen and statues show the skill of craftspeople. Lapis lazuli from Afghanistan and ebony and ivory from the south show trade with distant lands.

questions.question: What did the tomb reveal about daily life and family?
questions.expected_answer: Everyday objects such as linen clothes, sandals, walking sticks, fans, beds, headrests, board games like senet, musical instruments, food and labelled wine jars show how people, at least the royal family, lived. A lock of his grandmother Queen Tiye's hair, images of his wife Ankhesenamun and the mummies of two baby daughters give clues about his family.
